Metformin XR · Model-Based Bioequivalence · PopPK surrogate

The comparison, set up fairly

PBPK side

PK-Sim mechanistic model → dense population profiles → NCA → BE endpoints. The reference answer.

PopPK side

Sparse-sample the same profiles, add 15% error, fit a 1-cmt Pumas model, re-simulate, NCA, BE. The surrogate.

Why the comparison is clean

Both pipelines feed identical statistics (be_utils.jl: TOST, VBE power, safe-space search). Any divergence in the BE decision therefore reflects the model — mechanistic vs empirical — not the test procedure.

Safe space overlay — AUC(inf)

Why AUC(inf) is the one endpoint to distrust here. AUCinf = AUCtEnd + Clast/λz. At slow release (T50 ≥ 6 h) the tablet is still absorbing at 24 h — flip-flop kinetics — so λz reflects absorption, not elimination, goes tiny, and the extrapolated tail blows up. In the GMR overlay this shows as the PBPK AUC(inf) curve climbing to ≈1.50 (T50 6) and ≈1.79 (T50 7), while PopPK falls to ≈0.74.

It is an NCA extrapolation artifact, not real added exposure: AUCtEnd for the same batches goes down (less absorbed within 0–24 h). PBPK integrates the pathological tail literally (and drops subjects with unestimable λz — only n = 21 survive at T50 = 7); the empirical PopPK model regularizes it via apparent CL. This is why AUC(0–tEnd) is the preferred XR endpoint and AUC(inf) should not drive the slow-release BE decision.

Where — and why — they diverge

Agree (decision-driving)

  • Cmax safe space matches within ~0.05–0.10 h.
  • AUCtEnd and the joint criterion match closely.
  • GMR curves overlie across T50 = 1–7 h.

Diverge (non-driving)

  • AUCinf at high T50 (6–7 h).
  • Terminal extrapolation is noisy under flip-flop kinetics — the PopPK λz is estimated from sparse tails; PBPK integrates mechanistically.
  • Does not change the BE decision, which Cmax governs.

At T50 = 7 h, PBPK AUCinf GMR runs off (≈1.79, one arm with n = 21 usable) while PopPK stays bounded (≈0.74) — a clear artifact of extrapolating an absorption-limited tail, not a real exposure difference.

Headline

Decision equivalence holds.

~0.05–0.15 h

agreement in safe-space boundaries between PBPK and PopPK, across all endpoints and both sample sizes.

So what

  • A cheap, data-driven PopPK surrogate reproduces the mechanistic PBPK BE conclusions for metformin XR.
  • Cmax drives the decision on both sides; the safe space is Cmax-limited at ~T50 1.8–4.1 h.
  • Only caveat: don't lean on AUCinf for slow-release batches — flip-flop makes it unstable in both frameworks, worst in PopPK.
